updates.note: Explained Zulu: channel shut, anchored ships to sea, two ships staying alongside with approval.
Said terminals have secured cargo operations; nothing restarts until surveys and dock inspections.
Said surge and wind carried the oil out of the channel; boom goes first where it protects the most shoreline.
Advised fishers and shoreline owners to start keeping photographs, trip logs and receipts before any claims process exists.
Said the fishing and shellfish closures stay until testing shows the water and catch are clean; urged fishers to keep records of losses.
Confirmed inspections aboard both tankers are complete and both are held at the berth; would not discuss cause.
Said Rendal Terminals is cooperating fully with the Unified Command and investigators.
Said the designation is about who pays for the response; cause is a separate, open investigation.
Repeated advice to keep records ahead of a claims process.
Urged people with oiled property or cleanup costs to file with the owners' claims center; told fishers to keep trip logs and landing records.
Confirmed the Captain of the Port order is still in effect for both tankers; gave no date.
Said 'contained' means the slick is no longer spreading, not that shorelines are clean or the bays reopen.
Called it a partial reopening and nothing else: outer and bay reaches open, inner channel restricted, queue worked by priority.
Called the close of the emergency phase a real milestone; said fishing closures are a separate decision that follows test results.
Said rescues, shelters and water come first; photograph damage when it is safe.
Apologized that a month is a long time to boil water; parts are coming from out of state.
Said lower stomach-illness numbers are not a reason to stop boiling.
Read the city's update twice looking for a date; wants a calendar.
Announced the Spanish-language option on the FEMA information line and bilingual outreach teams at shelters.
